source.title: Where are the call records?
source.intro: pbx reads the call records (CDR) of your Asterisk and changes nothing on it.
source.mysql.hint: The CDR database, such as FreePBX's asteriskcdrdb
files.label: Where are Master.csv and the recordings?
files.local.hint: A copy, or a shared folder
files.sftp.hint: pbx reads them over SSH and copies nothing else
sftp.title: Connect to the PBX over SFTP
sftp.intro: The user only needs to read the call records and the recordings.
sftp.host.hint: Its host name or IP address, as this computer reaches it.
password.hint: The password goes straight to pbx and is kept in your system's password store, or in the tool's own folder when there is none. It is kept only once the check works.
key.hint: Leave it empty the first time: the check shows the server's key. Compare it on the server with `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub`, then paste it here.
csv.title: Where is Master.csv?
csv.path.hint: On the PBX it is usually /var/log/asterisk/cdr-csv/Master.csv. Copy it here or share its folder, then type its path on this computer.
csv.path.remote.hint: Its path on the PBX, usually /var/log/asterisk/cdr-csv/Master.csv.
db.title: Connect to the CDR database
db.intro: pbx connects with this user and reads the newest hour of calls. It changes nothing.
db.host.hint: Its host name or IP address, as this computer reaches it.
db.port.hint: Leave empty for 3306 on MySQL or 5432 on PostgreSQL.
db.name: Database name
db.user.hint: A user that can only read the CDR table is enough.
db.tls.hint: Checks the server's certificate. Turn it on when the database is not on your own network.
db.ssh.title: Through an SSH tunnel (optional)
db.ssh.intro: When the database listens only on the PBX itself, as in FreePBX, pbx reaches it through the PBX's SSH server. The database server above is then the address as the PBX sees it, usually 127.0.0.1. Leave this empty to connect directly.
db.ssh.host-key: SSH server key (optional the first time)
rec.title: Recordings and numbers
rec.path.hint: The call recordings on this computer, such as a copy of /var/spool/asterisk/monitor. Calls come in without it too.
rec.path.remote.hint: The recordings' folder on the PBX, usually /var/spool/asterisk/monitor. Calls come in without it too.
region.label: Countries of your phone lines
region.hint: Callers are matched to your contacts by phone number. Asterisk often writes a number without its country code, so pick the countries your phone lines serve. Calls from other countries arrive with their + code anyway.
names.label: Names of the extensions (optional)
names.hint: Who answers on each internal number, as number=name pairs separated by commas. Without them, an extension is named only by its caller ID when it places a call, or by FreePBX. A name here wins over both.
check.title: Checking the connection
check.body: pbx reads the newest hour of calls to check the settings. It changes nothing. The passwords are kept only once that check works.
failed.title: The check failed
failed.body: pbx could not read the call records with these settings. Nothing was saved. Go back to change them.
done.title: Connected
done.body: Sync then brings in the calls of the last 30 days as meetings, with their recordings. The time zone of the records and the recordings' file names are settings of their own.
req.ffmpeg: ffmpeg, to read WAV and GSM recordings
req.ffmpeg.fix: Install ffmpeg with your system's package manager.
req.model: A speech model, to turn recordings into text
req.model.fix: Run once in a terminal: `pbx models download gigaam-v3`
